title: SEO: /just-added/ is linked from the homepage but has no route
description: homepage.html:23 links to /just-added/ and site/templates/just_added.html exists, but there is no @app.route for it and no freezer generator. On a frozen static site that is a hard 404 from the most-crawled page.
acceptance_criteria: Either the route + freezer generator + sitemap entry exist and /just-added/ builds, or the homepage link is removed. No dead internal links.
notes:
CORRECTION to the audit finding: /just-added/ is NOT a live 404. The homepage link at homepage.html:23 sits inside {% if recently_added %}, and 'recently_added' is never populated anywhere in calgen (grep: only the two homepage.html references exist). Verified against a frozen build - the string 'just-added' appears nowhere in the output HTML. So there is no crawlable broken link and no SEO harm today.

What is actually here is a half-built feature: just_added.html is complete, the homepage preview block is complete, .content-container/.added-day CSS is in main.css, but there is no route, no freezer generator, and no data source.

BLOCKER on finishing it: the page needs a per-event 'when was this added' date. Every event does have one - DynamoDB EVENT#<guid>/SK=META carries createdAt for ical-sourced events too - but export_dynamo_to_calgen.py:109 lists createdAt in the 'internal' drop tuple, so it never reaches calgen. Worse, ical events are not written to _single_events at all (only source in manual/submitted/None), so un-dropping the field is not sufficient; the export would need a new artifact such as _data/added_at.json mapping guid -> createdAt across all EVENT# META items.

That is exactly the index cdk_next/lambda_src/updates_publisher/app.py:_added_at_index already builds for the weekly /updates post (bead next_dctech_events-hiy, currently uncommitted work in progress). It also needs that file's (date,title) fallback, because submitted events get a different guid on the site than in DynamoDB (bead next_dctech_events-p8o).

DECISION: left the template, CSS and homepage block untouched rather than deleting a feature that is mid-flight elsewhere, and did not build a second createdAt pipeline alongside hiy. No SEO work is outstanding here. Landmine to note: whoever populates 'recently_added' turns homepage.html:23 into a real 404 unless the route lands in the same change.
close_reason: Closed

description:

title: Close public Cognito sign-ups
description:
Set AllowAdminCreateUserOnly=true on the shared user pool so the SignUp endpoint is closed and only AdminCreateUser can make accounts.

Safe to change: it is a mutable UserPool property, unlike Schema/UsernameAttributes, so it does not force replacement of the pool holding 66 real accounts. Existing users keep signing in.

Made possible by the magic-link submission flow — a self-service account no longer buys a submitter anything, and the open endpoint was absorbing sustained bot registrations.
acceptance_criteria: Public sign-up via hosted UI or the SignUp API is rejected; existing users can still sign in; admins can still be created with AdminCreateUser.
close_reason: Closed

title: Magic-link event submission (drop Cognito requirement)
description:
Submitting an event currently requires a Cognito account, which is a large barrier for a one-off submitter. Replace it with an emailed magic link: the user enters an email, receives a signed link, and can submit without ever creating an account.

Token is a KMS HMAC over email+timestamp, matching the newsletter confirmation-link precedent in NextNewsletterStack — stateless, so no session table or cleanup. /api/submissions and the new /api/submit-link drop the API Gateway Cognito authorizer and validate the token in Lambda instead; Cognito claims still work so admins and existing signed-in users are unaffected.

Because /api/submit-link sends mail to an arbitrary address, it needs a per-email cooldown or it is an open relay for filling someone's inbox.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-out user can request a link, receive the email, click it, and submit an event that lands in the moderation queue with their email as submitter; expired/tampered tokens are rejected; repeated link requests for one address are rate-limited; admin flows still work via Cognito.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed; verified end-to-end in production

title: Fix invalid JSON-LD escaping in event templates
description: Google Search Console reports 'unparseable structured data, Bad escape sequence in string'. The ItemList JSON-LD blocks use a hand-rolled {{ x | replace('"', '\\"') }} escaper that fights Jinja autoescape: the inserted quote becomes ", leaving \" (invalid JSON escape). Titles with & also render as literal & in the ingested value. Fix by using the tojson filter, which emits its own quotes, escapes correctly, and is script-safe.
notes: Fix committed as 3d80077 (site/templates/homepage.html, virtual_events.html: tojson). Verified by rendering both templates with adversarial titles — all 4 ld+json blocks parse, values round-trip exactly. cdk_next/build/site_src rebuilt via build_lambdas.sh; cdk diff clean (only S3 asset hash). BLOCKED on 'cdk deploy NextSiteGeneratorStack --exclusively' (denied by permission classifier) — CodeBuild source is a CDK S3 asset, so start-build alone rebuilds from stale templates. Note: CDK CLI must be npx -y aws-cdk@latest; the cached 2.1119.0 rejects schema 54.
close_reason: Deployed and verified live 2026-08-06. Build 60354c57 SUCCEEDED, CloudFront invalidation completed; all 4 ld+json blocks on / , /virtual/ and www parse, and the previously-broken title round-trips as '"Am I?" Film Screening & Discussion'.

title: build_lambdas.sh shipped stale calgen from uv cache
description:
calgen's version is pinned at 0.1.0 and never changes, so uv treated the locally-built wheel as cache-valid and reused it even after packages/calgen source changed. Lambda bundles and the CodeBuild wheel silently shipped pre-edit code.

Caught while working next_dctech_events-7lg: the deployed iCal aggregator contained zero references to HORIZON_DAYS after a clean build_lambdas.sh run and deploy, so the 180-day horizon had no effect in production despite the source being correct and passing local tests (the local venv uses an editable install, which reads source directly and therefore masked the problem).

Fixed by forcing a rebuild in all three places calgen is packaged:
  CALGEN_FRESH=(--refresh-package calgen --reinstall-package calgen)  # both uv pip install targets
  uv build --no-cache ...                                            # CodeBuild wheel

## Context
Worth remembering: an editable install in cdk_next/.venv means local pytest and local calgen builds always see current source, so this class of bug cannot be caught locally — only by inspecting the built artifact or the deployed function.
acceptance_criteria: After editing packages/calgen source, ./build_lambdas.sh produces bundles and a wheel containing the edit. Verified by grepping build/ical_aggregator/calgen, build/newsletter/calgen, and the built wheel.

title: db.py drops skip_phrases when reading GROUP items
description:
_group_item_to_dict in cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py copies a fixed allowlist of fields off the GROUP# item:

    for field in ['website', 'ical', 'fallback_url', 'categories',
                  'suppress_urls', 'suppress_guid', 'scan_for_metadata', 'url_override']:

skip_phrases is absent, so the field is silently discarded on every read even though put_group writes it and the migration carried it over from _groups/*.yaml (nvtc.yaml sets it). Anything reading groups through this helper — the site-generator export, the iCal aggregator, and the MCP list_groups tool — never sees it.

## Context
Introduced when backend/db.py was forked for this stack. One-line fix, but it blocks any skip_phrases support in calgen from taking effect.
acceptance_criteria: skip_phrases survives a get_group/get_all_groups round-trip and reaches _groups/*.yaml via export_dynamo_to_calgen.py.

title: Cap iCal fetch horizon at 180 days
description:
The vendored calgen has no upper bound on how far ahead it keeps iCal events, so dctech.events currently lists events out to 2029. The pre-cutover site capped them at 180 days.

In packages/calgen/src/calgen/calendars.py, fetch_ical_and_extract_events expands each VEVENT with an rrule individually over a 90-day window (recurring_end_dt) but applies no horizon at all to non-recurring events. Upstream replaced this with a single whole-calendar expansion bounded at 180 days:

    start_dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    end_dt = start_dt + timedelta(days=180)
    for event in recurring_ical_events.of(cal).between(start_dt, end_dt):

Measured against the live AFCEA feed: the current code yields 76 events through 2027-06, the 180-day form yields 39 through 2027-01.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit ce08c53 lineage), fetchable from the local checkout at ~/projects/calgen. Never ported when calgen was vendored, because the vendored copy came from a local working tree that predated it.
acceptance_criteria: Events beyond 180 days no longer appear on dctech.events. The iCal aggregator's prune step removes the now-out-of-horizon EVENT# items on its next run (expect roughly 96 removals). Site build succeeds and the homepage/month pages still render.

title: list_pending_qa limit is silently ignored
description:
`list_pending_qa(limit=N)` returns every pending event regardless of N, so
there is no way to run a bounded QC pass. Found while dry-running the QC agent
on 2026-08-26: invoked with {"limit": 10}, the agent logged "36 events pending
QC" and reviewed all 36.

CAUSE (verified): db.get_events_by_review_status (cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py
:463-473) does

    if limit:
        kwargs['Limit'] = limit
    items = _query_all(table, **kwargs)

DynamoDB's `Limit` caps items *per page*, and `_query_all` (db.py:56-62) then
follows LastEvaluatedKey until the query is exhausted. So Limit=10 means "10
per page, fetch every page" — the opposite of what the caller asked for, and
it fails silently.

WHY IT MATTERS: `limit` exists so a new prompt can be evaluated against a
handful of events instead of the whole queue. Without it, every dry run is a
full-queue pass — slower, more expensive, and more likely to hit the Bedrock
read timeouts that killed the 2026-08-26 dry run. It is the difference between
a two-minute test and a fifteen-minute one.

FIX: truncate after paginating, or stop paginating once enough rows are in
hand. Slicing the result is the smaller change and keeps `_query_all` general:

    items = _query_all(table, **kwargs)
    if limit:
        items = items[:limit]

Leaving `Limit` in kwargs is still worth it — it keeps the per-page read cost
down even though it does not bound the total.

CHECK THE OTHER CALLERS before changing this: get_events_by_review_status is
shared by the MCP server, the API and the discovery agent's proposal queue, so
confirm none of them are relying on the current all-rows behaviour while
passing a limit. Grep for get_events_by_review_status and for the MCP tools
list_pending_qa / list_discovery_proposals.

Same shape may exist elsewhere — audit other `kwargs['Limit']` uses next to
_query_all / _scan_all in db.py.

title: Normalize doubled 'City, ST' in iCal event locations
description:
Many EVENT# locations end with a repeated `City, ST`, so listings display a
city and state twice.

Observed in the pending QC queue (2026-08-26):

  a82752cd… "Rockville Memorial Library, Rockville Town Square Plaza,
             21 Maryland Ave, Rockville, MD, Rockville, MD"
  8ea07ae7… "Fuse At Mason Square, 3351 Fairfax Drive,, Arlington, VA,
             Arlington, VA"
  13a742bc… "Barbara M. Donnellan Auditorium, 1015 N Quincy St.,
             Arlington, va, Arlington, va"      <- lowercase state
  40f001f0… "HacDC, 3333 14th St NW, Suite M110, Washington, DC,
             Washington, DC"

Spans many groups, which is what makes it a pipeline issue rather than
organiser typos.

CAUSE (verified): Meetup's own iCal LOCATION property already ends in
`City, ST`, and Meetup appends city and state again. calgen passes the value
through verbatim — packages/calgen/src/calgen/calendars.py:206-207,
`resolved_location = ical_location`.

NOT the cause: the JSON-LD address join at calendars.py:96-101. That branch
only fires when the iCal LOCATION is empty (see the `if not ical_location`
guard at :216), so it is not involved in these cases.

BLAST RADIUS is display only — I checked. `location_utils.extract_location_info`
reads from the end of the string and normalizes case, so region faceting and
/locations/ are unaffected:
  extract_location_info("… Arlington, va, Arlington, va") -> ('Arlington', 'VA')
Purely cosmetic, hence P2 rather than higher.

FIX DIRECTION: normalize once at parse time in calendars.py, before the value
reaches `event_data`. Collapse a trailing repeat of the final `City, ST`, and
while there, squeeze the doubled commas Meetup also emits ("3351 Fairfax
Drive,,"). Doing it at parse time means the stored value is clean and no
consumer has to defend against it.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING even though it is cosmetic: the QC polish pass
(next_dctech_events-wm4 follow-on) is now pointed at exactly this kind of
location defect. A one-time normalizer removes the work permanently; leaving it
means paying a model call every week to correct machine-generated noise.

SEPARATE PROBLEM, do not conflate: 13a742bc's sibling 8ea07ae7/dd0d5c82
("DevFest DC 2026") carries "Arlington, DC" — Arlington is in Virginia. That is
Meetup's own wrong addressRegion, so normalization cannot fix it; it currently
files the event under Washington DC. Needs the polish pass or a human.

title: Overlay edits should trigger site rebuilds
description:
The DynamoDB-streams-fed site build trigger (dctech-events-next-site-build-trigger) only watches for changes to keys with prefixes: EVENT#, GROUP#, CATEGORY#, RECURRING#, ICAL#, POST#, UPDATE#.

Overlay writes use a different key prefix and are therefore invisible to the trigger, meaning a hidden/modified event stays live on the site until the next scheduled build.

This is especially important for the QA agent, which hides cancelled events via overlays — those changes should publish immediately.

Fix: add the OVERLAY# key prefix (or whatever prefix overlays use) to RELEVANT_PREFIXES in handler.py of dctech-events-next-site-build-trigger.

Discovered while manually hiding AFCEA Belvoir August 2026 Luncheon *** Cancelled *** (guid: 653c72128c89e69b95fb01687e369936) and having to force-invoke CodeBuild directly.

title: Set production Tavily key for discovery agent
description: Discovery runtime secret dctech-events-next/discovery/tavily currently contains a placeholder/generated value. Set a valid Tavily API key so open-web search tools succeed (tavily_search/tavily_extract currently return Unauthorized in runtime logs).

title: Handle cancelled events from iCal feeds
description:
The iCal ingestion pipeline currently imports events even when they are cancelled. Cancellation can appear in two ways:

1. iCal standard: STATUS:CANCELLED property on the VEVENT
2. Source-specific: title contains '*** Cancelled ***' (seen with AFCEA Belvoir Eventbrite feed)

The QA agent should detect events with these signals and either skip them during ingestion or flag/hide them automatically.

Example: AFCEA Belvoir August 2026 Luncheon *** Cancelled *** (guid: 653c72128c89e69b95fb01687e369936) — was manually hidden via overlay on 2026-08-24.

Suggested approach:
- During iCal processing, check VEVENT STATUS:CANCELLED and skip those events
- Also filter titles matching case-insensitive pattern like '\*\*\* cancel' 
- For already-imported cancelled events, the QA agent should identify and hide them via overlay

title: SEO: per-event landing pages that route users to the primary source
description: Every event links straight out (events_by_day.html:21), so the site has no indexable URL for any individual event and cannot rank for long-tail queries like 'kubernetes meetup arlington'. The homepage ItemList JSON-LD (homepage.html:55-106) is also ineligible for Google event rich results: items lack their own url on this domain, a full PostalAddress, and endDate.
design:
HARD CONSTRAINT: this site sends users to primary sources immediately and must not become a 'roach motel' calendar. Design rules, all required:

1. List pages keep linking directly out. events_by_day.html:21 is unchanged - the event TITLE always points at the organizer's URL, target=_blank.
2. The event page is a SEARCH LANDING PAGE, not a step in the site's own click path. It serves people arriving from Google who had no direct path to intercept.
3. Internal discovery is via a low-prominence permalink (a '#' glyph or the timestamp) beside the title, blog-permalink style. Crawlers follow it; users who want the event never click it. Orphan pages do not rank, so some internal link is required - the resolution is prominence, not presence.
4. On the event page the primary source link is THE primary action: above the fold, largest affordance, organizer's real hostname visible. No redirect interstitial, no click wrapper, no signup wall - a direct href.
5. Do NOT republish the organizer's description (available at calendars.py:231). That is both the substitution behavior we object to and duplicate content that would get the page filtered. Show facts only: when, where, who, categories.
6. Earn the page's existence with information the source does not have: also_published_by (which other groups list this event), a per-event .ics download, category cross-links, and persistence after the source link rots. Pairs with the archive work in the sibling issue.
7. Event JSON-LD: url points at our page (that is what earns the rich result); the source goes in offers.url, which is where Google routes 'register' clicks anyway. Include startDate, endDate, full PostalAddress, organizer, eventAttendanceMode, eventStatus.

Considered and rejected: anchor IDs on existing week/month pages. Honest and nearly free, but Google rarely ranks a fragment URL independently and per-event Event schema cannot attach cleanly to a 40-event page. Roughly a tenth of the upside.
acceptance_criteria: /events/<slug>/ pages freeze for every current event, carry valid Event structured data, appear in the sitemap, and are reachable only via the low-prominence permalink. Outbound behavior on all list pages is byte-identical to before except for the added permalink. Event descriptions from feeds are not republished.
close_reason: Closed

title: SEO: keep past month and week pages instead of letting them 404
description: get_upcoming_months() (app.py:629) derives months from current events only, and get_upcoming_weeks(12) bounds weeks the same way. Past month and week pages stop being generated and their URLs start 404ing, so accumulated links and rankings for e.g. /2026/6/ die on a monthly schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Past month and week pages stay frozen as archives, appear in the sitemap with an honest lastmod and changefreq never, and are reachable by an internal link. No previously-published URL 404s after a rebuild.
notes:
Investigated; needs a design decision before implementation. Confirmed the harm is real: site_generator_stack.py:52 deploys with 'aws s3 sync build/ --delete', so a month page that stops being generated is actively deleted from the bucket and returns a hard 404.

Why this is not a small fix: there is no historical event data anywhere in the pipeline. pipeline.py:304 and :328 drop events with event_date < today at ingest, and the ical cache only ever holds what the organizer's feed currently advertises - once an event passes, the source feed drops it and calgen has already discarded it. So past month/week pages cannot be rebuilt from anything on disk.

The weekly /updates roundups looked like an existing archive, but updates.py's module docstring rules that out going forward: as of 2026-08-12 roundups list the events ADDED that week, not the events HAPPENING that week. Only pre-2026-08-12 posts are 'what happened' snapshots.

The build is ephemeral CodeBuild (site_generator_stack.py BUILDSPEC) regenerating _data from a DynamoDB export each run, so any archive needs new persistent storage (S3 object or DynamoDB items) plus pipeline merge logic plus freezer generators plus a stack change for permissions.

Options put to the user 2026-08-13:
  a) Real archives - persist past events to a new store; accumulates from the change forward, cannot recover history already lost.
  b) Archive stubs - calgen enumerates every month/week from site launch to today and emits a 200 page saying the events have passed, linking to /updates and current listings. No new storage; deterministic; thin, so noindex+follow to preserve link flow without indexing near-duplicates.
  c) Accept the 404s.

Rejected as unworkable: scoping the s3 sync --delete to spare past paths. --exclude applies to source and destination alike, so sparing /2026/8/ from deletion would also stop it updating while it is still the current month, and the pattern cannot distinguish past from current.
IMPLEMENTED as variant A (publisher-side), per user 2026-08-13. The earlier 'needs new persistent storage' framing was wrong: _updates/ is already a DynamoDB export (export_dynamo_to_calgen.py:152), so the durable store already existed.

Publisher (updates_publisher/app.py): added _next_week_bounds, _events_in_week, _archive_item. Each Wednesday run now also writes ARCHIVE#<week_id>/SK=META for the FOLLOWING ISO week, computed from the events.json it already fetches - no new source, no new fetch, no IAM change. Guarded on today (not publish_date) so a backdated manual re-run cannot overwrite a good capture with an empty one.
Export: ARCHIVE items land in _archive/{week_id}.yaml. by_prefix is generic over PK prefix and filters SK==META, so no scan change was needed.
calgen: new archive.py (get_archived_weeks/week/events, merge_events). Week and month routes merge live + archived, live winning on conflict. get_all_week_ids/get_all_months drive the freezer and sitemap so past pages keep building.
Templates: archive-notice on past week/month pages; permalinks withheld from archived events since /events/ pages exist only for current events.
Also fixed a pre-existing bug the archive exposed: month prev/next nav linked to months that were never frozen (has_prev/has_next now gate it).

Known limits, by design: coverage starts when archiving starts - months already lost stay lost; a capture is taken up to a week ahead, so events added after it are missing (same fidelity the weekly email has). Variant B (site generator refreshes archives every build) closes that gap but needs a table write permission on the CodeBuild role.
close_reason: Closed

title: SEO: noindex thin category-month facet pages
description: The sidebar cross-links every category with every month and freeze.py:54 materializes each combo. Combos holding one or two events are thin near-duplicates competing with their parent /categories/<slug>/ page.
acceptance_criteria: Category-month pages below an event threshold emit robots noindex,follow (or canonical to the parent category). Substantial ones are in the sitemap. Same treatment for zero-event location pages.
close_reason: Closed

title: SEO: add og:image and favicon assets
description: base.html:32-55 has all image/icon tags commented out pending a HEADER_IMAGES.md that does not exist in the repo. site/static/images/ holds only a README and a sizes reference. Every social share renders as a bare text link and Google's mobile results show a blank favicon.
acceptance_criteria: A 1200x630 OG card and a favicon set exist under site/static/images/, the commented-out tags in base.html are live, and site/static/manifest.json.template is resolved.
close_reason: Closed

title: Submitted events get a different guid on the site than in DynamoDB
description: db.put_event keys submitted events EVENT#<8 hex> but calgen's load_single_events unconditionally recomputes guid = calculate_event_hash(date,time,title,url) (pipeline.py:167), so events.json shows a 32-char guid for them. Consequences: _overlay/<dynamo-guid>.yaml never matches a submitted event, so overrides on submissions silently do nothing; and anything joining events.json back to the table by guid misses them (the updates publisher works around it with a date+title fallback). Fix is probably for load_single_events to honor a guid already present in the YAML and for the exporter to write it.

title: Render the new post shape in calgen
description: updates.py: honor published_on and an explicit stored summary; update_post.html: do not label a newly-added roundup as 'this week'.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested; verified end to end against live data with a local calgen build (23 events, /updates/2026/8/12/ renders).

title: QC: build calendar_qc asset (ARM64)
description: build_lambdas.sh: replace the qa_agent stub arm with a calendar_qc target installing strands-agents, strands-agents-tools[agent_core_browser], bedrock-agentcore, mcp, requests. MUST use aarch64-manylinux_2_17 — AgentCore Runtime is Graviton-only and the script's PLATFORM is x86_64.
close_reason: build_lambdas.sh builds build/calendar_qc with aarch64 wheels (--only-binary :all: so a source build fails loudly rather than shipping x86_64 to Graviton). Verified ELF is ARM aarch64; 280M unpacked / 92M zipped vs 750M/250M limits. Split the old qa_agent stub arm into discovery_agent + new qa_trigger.

title: MCP tools for reviewing and approving submissions
description:
The MCP server can create content but cannot see or act on the moderation queue, so triaging submissions requires the /edit UI. Add tools mirroring the REST admin routes: list_pending_submissions, get_submission, approve_submission (with optional trust_submitter), reject_submission, and list/trust/untrust_submitter.

Promotion logic currently lives in routes/admin.py, which the MCP Lambda does not bundle. Move it into db.py so the REST handlers and MCP share one implementation rather than growing a second copy of the approval rules.

Accepted trust boundary: MCP is IAM-authed for trusted agents and has no per-user admin check, unlike the REST routes. Confirmed acceptable — the endpoint already exposes add_single_event and set_overlay, so this is consistent with the existing boundary.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can list the pending queue, inspect a draft, approve it (optionally trusting the submitter), and reject it; approval promotes to EVENT#/GROUP# and marks the draft approved exactly as the REST route does; approval logic exists in one place; trusted submitters can be listed, added, and revoked.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in production: 7 moderation tools on the MCP server, promotion logic consolidated into db.promote_draft, 34 new tests

title: Email the admin on every event submission
description: Send ross@karchner.com an immediate email whenever an event or group is submitted, complementing the daily queue digest in NextOpsStack. Auto-published submissions from trusted submitters are included, since those never reach the queue and the mail is the only signal they happened.
acceptance_criteria: Every submission path emails the admin; the mail names the event, submitter, and whether it is queued or already published; Reply-To is the submitter; an SES failure never fails the submission.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed; verified no send failures in production logs after two live submissions

title: Trusted submitters: auto-approve future submissions
description:
Add a 'trust this submitter' option to the approval flow. Once trusted, that person's later event submissions skip the moderation queue and publish immediately.

Trust is keyed by normalized email, which is the only stable identity across both auth paths (magic-link submitters have submitter_id 'magiclink:<email>' and no Cognito sub). This is safe because the magic-link flow proves control of the address before a submission is accepted — an attacker cannot submit as a trusted address without receiving that address's mail.

Auto-approved submissions still write a DRAFT record for the audit trail, then immediately promote and mark APPROVED with an automated reviewer, so the queue history stays complete and the EVENT# write triggers the usual rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: Approving with the trust box ticked records the submitter as trusted; that submitter's next event submission publishes without entering the queue and is visible in history as auto-approved; admins can list and revoke trusted submitters; untrusted submitters are unaffected; group submissions still require review.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in production: trust checkbox on approve, auto-approval of trusted submitters' events, admin list/revoke UI, 37 new tests

title: Newsletter opt-in checkbox on the event submission form
description:
Add a 'sign me up for the weekly newsletter' checkbox to the event submission form. When ticked, subscribe the submitter to the SES contact list.

No double opt-in confirmation email is needed here: the magic-link flow (or Cognito) has already proven the submitter controls that address, which is exactly what the newsletter confirmation link exists to establish. Subscribing directly avoids making the user confirm the same address twice in one flow.
acceptance_criteria: Ticking the box subscribes the submitter to the dctech topic on the newsletter contact list; leaving it unticked subscribes nobody; an SES failure does not fail the event submission.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed; verified end-to-end in production

title: Free-form posts on /updates with an /edit management tool
description:
Add a second kind of /updates post: hand-written, Markdown-bodied announcements (e.g. 'I've added support for recurring events'), alongside the automated weekly roundups. Free-form posts live at /updates/<slug>/ and interleave with weekly posts in the /updates/ index and RSS feed.

Authoring is via a new admin-gated posts manager in /edit, backed by CRUD routes under /api/admin/posts (the api_stack already proxies /api/admin/*, so no CDK route change). Drafts are visible in /edit but never rendered.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create/edit/delete a Markdown post in /edit; published posts render at /updates/<slug>/ and appear in the index and feed ordered with weekly posts; drafts never render; tests cover the model, slug handling, and draft filtering.
close_reason: Implemented: markdown free-form posts at /updates/<slug>/, admin CRUD API, /edit posts manager, draft filtering. 52 calgen tests + 12 publisher tests pass.

title: Point updates.dctech.events at dctech.events/updates
description: The new first-party /updates section replaces the external Bear Blog. Once the first posts are live, updates.dctech.events should redirect to https://dctech.events/updates/ so existing links and RSS subscribers follow over. Needs a Route53 record plus a redirect (CloudFront function or S3 redirect bucket) — deliberately not done as part of the feature build since it changes a live external hostname.
acceptance_criteria: updates.dctech.events/ 301s to dctech.events/updates/; old post URLs at minimum land on the index.
close_reason: Not wanted: no interest in archival content or the old domain (2026-08-08)

title: Add /updates weekly blog to replace updates.dctech.events
description:
Replace the external Bear Blog at updates.dctech.events with a first-party /updates section on dctech.events. A post is published for each ISO week, titled 'DC Tech Events for the week of <Monday>', linking to that week's /week/<id>/ page and summarizing the events.

Key design decision: the static site is fully regenerated by calgen/Frozen-Flask every 4 hours and on DynamoDB change, so posts are DERIVED from ISO weeks rather than written by a Monday cron. A week's post becomes visible as soon as its Monday arrives — no new scheduled infrastructure, no stored post records, and the archive is reproducible from event data alone.
acceptance_criteria: /updates/ index lists posts newest-first; /updates/<y>/<m>/<d>/ renders a per-week post linking to /week/<id>/; /updates/feed.xml is a valid RSS feed for reader migration; future weeks are never published; nav and sitemap include /updates/; tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented: calgen /updates index + per-week post pages + RSS, snapshot-based publisher Lambda on a Monday cron, export wiring, nav/sitemap/CSS. 49 tests pass; verified end-to-end via Frozen-Flask build and cdk synth.

title: Add Mastodon and Bluesky credential secrets
description: Provision two Secrets Manager secrets in a new NextSocialStack to hold externally-issued social credentials: a Mastodon API access token and Bluesky credentials (handle + app password). Values are populated manually out-of-band; CDK only creates the placeholder secrets and exposes them as stack attributes for a future posting Lambda to grant_read.
acceptance_criteria: NextSocialStack exists with mastodon_secret and bluesky_secret attributes; wired into app.py; cdk synth succeeds; no generated values for externally-issued credentials.
close_reason: NextSocialStack created with mastodon + bluesky secrets (RETAIN, JSON placeholder shape), wired into app.py, synth verified

title: Migration created ~31 duplicate events under mismatched guid schemes
description:
scripts/migrate_to_next_table.py reconciled the git YAML and the old dctech-events table by guid ('YAML wins on collision'), but the two sources never shared a guid scheme: calgen derives md5(date,time,title,url) while the old table's EVENT# items carried uuid-style ids. Same logical event, different key, so the collision check never fired and both copies were imported.

The migration report at the time ('62 copied verbatim') therefore understated the problem — roughly half of those 62 were duplicates of events that already existed under a calgen guid.

Surfaced as 'Also published by None' on the site: calgen's remove_duplicates merged the pair at render time and credited the duplicate's group, which was null for manual events.

Fixed 2026-08-02: 31 redundant records deleted (backed up to .backup-predecom-20260802/deleted-duplicate-events.json), keeping the calgen-canonical record of each pair. Legitimate co-publishing between iCal groups was deliberately left intact.
acceptance_criteria: No two EVENT# records share a title+date with no group. Any future migration reconciles on canonical event identity, not raw guid.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cognito pool is taking sustained signup spam
description:
As of 2026-08-02, 51 of 66 accounts in us-east-1_8Ay4dTt8j were UNCONFIRMED, all created within about six days. The pattern is automated abuse, not real signups:

  - dot-injected Gmail aliases: l.i.z.a.g.ey.e.r.ma.n@gmail.com, r.ad.t.ech.mom.o@gmail.com, n.o.kia.fl.o.of.22@gmail.com
  - spoofed corporate domains: questions@valvesoftware.com, paypal@wwt.it
  - unrelated org domains: yuroktribe.nsn.us, leacounty.net, lift-texas.net

Only ~15 accounts are confirmed. The pool has selfSignUpEnabled with the hosted UI publicly reachable at login.dctech.events, so anything can register. Each signup also triggers a Cognito verification email through the SES identity, which puts the domain's sending reputation at risk if bounce rates climb.

The new weekly pruner (dctech-events-next-cleanup-unconfirmed-users) clears them after 7 days, so this is contained but not prevented. Its MAX_DELETIONS guard is set to 1000 to avoid blocking on this volume.

Options: enable the Cognito advanced-security / bot detection features, put WAF in front of the hosted UI, or turn off self-signup and invite admins manually.

## Context
Found while re-creating the pruning job that was lost when dctech-events-api was deleted. Worth checking SES bounce/complaint rates for the dctech.events identity too.
acceptance_criteria: Either signup abuse is being blocked at the edge, or a conscious decision is recorded that pruning alone is sufficient.
notes:
Timing analysis settles what this is. Unconfirmed signups arrive 4-52 seconds apart across wholly unrelated domains (accountspayable@cbwm.org, questions@valvesoftware.com, jberling@yuroktribe.nsn.us within seconds of each other); 16 of 50 consecutive pairs are under 3 minutes. That is machine-paced, and the plausible-looking addresses are harvested third-party addresses, not registrations by their owners.

So the abuse is using Cognito as an email relay: the victims are the address owners, who receive unsolicited verification mail from dctech.events. That is what drives the complaint rate (0.07% against AWS's 0.1% review threshold), and it is why prevention beats pruning — pruning cannot unsend an email.

A PreSignUp trigger is now deployed in AUDIT mode (ENFORCE=false) in NextCognitoStack. Validated against the real pool export: 0 false positives on all 15 confirmed users, catches 19 of 51 unconfirmed (37%) via gmail dot-injection and disposable domains. It cannot catch the remaining 63% because those addresses are genuinely well-formed — only rate limiting can.

Next: (1) review audit logs, then set ENFORCE=true; (2) add WAF rate-based rules on the login.dctech.events hosted UI, which is now the primary control rather than a fallback.
close_reason: Resolved by closing public sign-ups (AllowAdminCreateUserOnly=true, deployed 2026-08-08) — the SignUp endpoint bots were hitting is now rejected outright. Verified with a live SignUp call returning NotAuthorizedException.

title: Port weekly cleanup of unconfirmed Cognito users
description:
The old dctech-events-api stack ran dctech-events-cleanup-unconfirmed-users on cron(0 2 ? * SUN *), deleting unconfirmed users from the shared pool us-east-1_8Ay4dTt8j. It last ran 2026-08-01 and was removed when that stack was deleted during decommissioning.

The pool is now adopted by this stack and still accumulates unconfirmed signups, so the hygiene job is still wanted. Source is in the old repo at cleanup_unconfirmed_users/handler.py; it needs cognito-idp:ListUsers and AdminDeleteUser on the pool.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled Lambda in this stack removes unconfirmed users older than the previous threshold, with the same weekly cadence.
close_reason: Closed

title: Normalize invisible Unicode in event titles
description:
Event titles arriving from iCal feeds can contain zero-width and other invisible Unicode characters. Left in place they break two things:

- skip_phrases matching, since a title with a zero-width space no longer matches the configured phrase
- duplicate detection, since are_events_duplicates in packages/calgen/src/calgen/pipeline.py compares titles exactly, and calculate_event_hash in event_utils.py folds the title into the guid — so the same event can churn guids or fail to dedupe

Upstream strips these characters in event_utils.py before hashing and in pipeline.py before comparison.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit 3c9246e, 'Fix invisible Unicode chars breaking skip_phrases filtering and duplicate detection'), fetchable from ~/projects/calgen. Note this changes guids for any affected event, so expect one-time churn: the aggregator will write new EVENT# items and prune the old ones. Upstream also ships tests/test_unicode_normalization.py worth porting alongside.
acceptance_criteria: Titles differing only by invisible characters produce the same guid and dedupe against each other; skip_phrases matching is unaffected by them.

title: Port skip_phrases group filtering into calgen
description:
Groups can declare skip_phrases to drop matching events from their feed. The vendored calgen ignores the field entirely, so those events publish. _groups/nvtc.yaml sets:

    skip_phrases:
      - COMMUNITY TUESDAYS AT REFRACTION

and roughly 15 such events are currently live on dctech.events; the pre-cutover site filtered them.

Upstream implements the match in packages/calgen/src/calgen/pipeline.py during event processing, case-insensitively against the event title.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit ce08c53), fetchable from ~/projects/calgen. Blocked by the db.py read bug — until that is fixed the field never reaches calgen even if the matching logic is ported.
acceptance_criteria: Events whose titles match a group's skip_phrases are absent from _data/all_events.json and the built site. The nvtc 'Community Tuesdays at Refraction' events stop appearing.
notes: Working as intended, with a correction to this ticket's premise. The nvtc feed publishes 2 'Community Tuesdays at Refraction' copies and skip_phrases now drops both. The 13 that remain on the site are source='recurring' — a curated RECURRING# definition expanded over 90 days — which group-level skip_phrases does not (and should not) touch. That is exactly why the phrase was configured: suppress the feed duplicates, keep the curated series. Live site now shows 13, matching the pre-cutover site's 13. The ticket's '~15 such events show' figure came from a grep that conflated occurrences.

title: QC polish pass should correct improbable city/state pairs
description:
Ask the QC polish pass to catch locations whose city and state cannot both be
right — "Arlington, DC" (Arlington is in Virginia), "Bethesda, VA", "Reston,
MD".

WHY IT MATTERS: this is not cosmetic, unlike the doubled-city issue in
next_dctech_events-8so. `location_utils.extract_location_info` reads the
trailing `City, ST`, so a wrong state silently files the event under the wrong
region facet:

  extract_location_info("… Arlington, DC, Arlington, DC") -> ('Washington','DC')

The event then appears under /locations/washington-dc/ instead of Northern
Virginia, and a reader filtering by region never sees it.

HOW COMMON: rare. I scanned all 338 EVENT# items (2026-08-26) against a table
of DC-area cities and found exactly one:

  dd0d5c82  "DevFest DC 2026 - Build Edition"  (Google Developer Group DC)
            "3351 Fairfax Dr, 3351 Fairfax Drive, Arlington, DC, Arlington, DC"

Source is Meetup's own addressRegion, so this is upstream content error rather
than a pipeline bug — nothing to normalize, it needs judgement. Filed P3 on
frequency, not on impact: worth having as a standing check because it fails
silently, but it is not urgent at one event.

That one event is also half of the duplicate pair 8ea07ae7 / dd0d5c82, so the
triage pass may hide it before polish ever looks at it. Do not treat its
disappearance as evidence this is fixed.

IMPLEMENTATION: a rule in POLISH_PROMPT (cdk_next/agents/calendar_qc/prompt.py).
Needs care, because the prompt currently says:

  "never change a location to move an event between cities — that is the
   out-of-area pass's decision, not yours"

Correcting Arlington, DC -> Arlington, VA does not move the event; it labels
the same place correctly. The rule needs an explicit carve-out saying so, or
the model will read the existing caution and leave it alone. Keep the
prohibition on actually relocating an event.

Worth pairing with a deterministic check instead of or alongside the prompt: a
city -> state table for the DC metro is small, and a mismatch is a fact rather
than a judgement. A validator in the aggregator or the MCP's set_overlay path
would catch it without a model call. The scan that found this used ~26 cities.

title: QC: duplicates that appear after approval are never re-checked
description: An event that becomes a duplicate AFTER approval (feed edits its title/date into collision) never re-enters the pending_qa queue, since the aggregator preserves review_status on refresh. The corpus-comparison design catches new-vs-existing but not this. Fix if it ever bites: a periodic full sweep ignoring the queue. Not worth building without evidence it happens.

title: Cross-post the Monday /updates post to Mastodon and Bluesky
description:
NextSocialStack already provisions the mastodon and bluesky credential secrets, and the updates publisher already produces exactly the content worth syndicating (title + link to the week). Extend the publisher (or add a follow-on target on the same Monday rule) to post the week's headline and /updates/ permalink to both networks after a successful publish.

Grant with social.mastodon_secret.grant_read(fn) / social.bluesky_secret.grant_read(fn); populate the secret values first (see the NextSocialStack docstring).
acceptance_criteria: A successful Monday publish posts once to each network; a failure to post does not block or duplicate the DynamoDB write.
close_reason: Stream-driven social publisher deployed; verified live on both networks

title: Backfill of past /updates weeks is not possible from current data
description:
The updates publisher snapshots a week from the site's events.json, but calgen's pipeline and get_events() both drop events dated before today, so events.json only ever contains upcoming events. Invoking the publisher with {"week_of": <past Monday>} therefore produces an empty post.

The archive can only build forward from the first real run. If historical posts matter, the content would have to come from the old Bear Blog export at updates.dctech.events, or from a DynamoDB point-in-time restore, and be written as UPDATE#<week_id> items directly.
acceptance_criteria: Decide whether historical posts are needed; if so, import them from the old blog export as UPDATE# items.
close_reason: Not wanted: no interest in archival content or the old domain (2026-08-08)

title: Drop deprecated CDK APIs: Route53 delete_existing and Stack.add_dependency
description: cdk synth emitted 8 deprecation warnings for aws_route53.RecordSetOptions#deleteExisting and one for Stack#addDependency. delete_existing existed only for the 2026-08-01 GitHub Pages cutover; it is now a live custom resource holding route53:DELETE on the production zone. Removed it and switched add_dependency to add_stack_dependency.
close_reason: Fixed in b04a5e6; cdk synth clean. NextHostingStack deploy still pending.

title: Decide fate of the daily submission-queue notification
description:
The old stack ran dctech-events-queue-notification daily at cron(30 13 * * ? *), emailing ross@karchner.com a summary of pending submissions. It was reading the OLD dctech-events table, so since the cutover it has been reporting on a table that no longer receives submissions — it last ran 2026-08-01 and went away with the dctech-events-api stack.

Either port it against dctech-events-next (GSI1 STATUS#pending) or consciously drop it. Nothing else currently notifies about a pending review queue.
acceptance_criteria: Either a scheduled notifier exists against the new table, or this is closed as won't-do with a note.
close_reason: Closed
